$schema_note: Experiment registry: one entry per experiment_id referenced from hypotheses.json. Acceptance/rejection criteria are drawn directly from TRD v1.1 FINAL's own evidentiary standard (sections 30, 49, 50 and the ablation protocol in docs/TEAM_CHARTER.md) -- no numeric thresholds are invented here (no 'p < 0.05', no specific EV/DD targets). That would be inventing performance requirements the spec does not state. 'shared_acceptance_criteria' and 'shared_rejection_criteria' apply to every experiment below; per-experiment fields only add what's specific to that comparison.
shared_acceptance_criteria: Untouched OOS EV_net for the variant exceeds the baseline's, with the reported uncertainty interval (Wilson for simple proportions, cluster/bootstrap where episodes are dependent) not spanning zero improvement.
Drawdown, ES/CVaR, and open MTM inventory for the variant are not worse than the baseline without a compensating EV gain that justifies the added risk.
Calibration (Brier/log-loss/reliability) for any model output used by the hypothesis is acceptable by the same standard as every other production model (TRD MODEL-003) -- not merely 'high WR'.

Sample size is reported as both raw N and independent-cluster N; per TRD section 50 a claim approaching the 70-80% range specifically needs ~300+ independent OOS episodes, preferably 500+ across regimes, before it can be treated as more than a preliminary signal.
The result survives clustered-bootstrap/regime resampling -- an effect that only appears in one regime or one narrow date range is not accepted as general.
Selection-bias diagnostics (DSR/PBO or equivalent) do not flag the finding as explainable by search breadth, given however many variants were actually tried.
shared_rejection_criteria: Untouched OOS EV_net is not positive, or its uncertainty interval spans zero or negative.
The effect only holds when the final untouched OOS period was used to select the threshold or feature that produced it (ML-002 violation) -- automatic rejection regardless of the reported number.
Drawdown/ES/CVaR worsens without a compensating EV gain.
The effect disappears under clustered-bootstrap/regime resampling or is flagged by DSR/PBO as consistent with selection bias.

The result was obtained by adjusting the model, threshold, or OOS split specifically to move the reported win rate toward the 70-80% range -- this is rejected on process grounds regardless of the resulting number, per the charter's explicit prohibition.

experiments.comparison: BQ-1 (premium/IV-rank-only selection) vs. A1 (B1 + ownership model), with B5 (random-entry matched) as the random-null reference.
experiments.specific_notes: This is TRD's own A1 ablation step, scoped to the CSP-entry decision specifically.

experiments.comparison: BQ-1 (IV-rank-only) vs. A1 (+ ownership model), same as EXP-Q-01 -- this experiment is the confirmatory read of the same ablation from the 'what goes wrong without ownership screening' angle rather than a separate run.
experiments.specific_notes: May be reported alongside EXP-Q-01 from the same A1 run rather than as an independent backtest.

experiments.comparison: BH-1 (conventional 30-60 DTE on the same names) vs. the 2-5 DTE Hold-the-Strike policy, with B5 as random-null.
experiments.specific_notes: Universe must be the specific, separately validated cohort TRD requires for this branch -- not the general universe.

experiments.comparison: BR-1 (always hold to expiration) vs. active close/roll variant, evaluated as part of A5 (dynamic management ablation), with B5 as random-null.
experiments.specific_notes: Must be run on the same candidate set and time period as EXP-R-02 so the two competing hypotheses are compared on equal footing, not cherry-picked periods.

experiments.comparison: BR-2 (fixed 50% profit-take close/roll) vs. hold-to-cycle variant, evaluated as part of A5, with B5 as random-null.
experiments.specific_notes: See EXP-R-01 -- same candidate set and period required for a fair head-to-head, since H-R-01 and H-R-02 directly contradict each other.

experiments.comparison: BR-1 (naive always-hold, as a stand-in for 'no explicit alternative comparison') vs. a policy that computes RollUtility against HOLD/CLOSE/ASSIGN/REDEPLOY at each decision timestamp (TRD Appendix A RollUtility formula), within A5.
experiments.specific_notes: This measures the *value of the discipline itself* (comparing alternatives) rather than picking a side in the R-01/R-02 debate.

experiments.comparison: BC-1 (max annualized yield CC selection) vs. full CCUtility-based selection (TRD section 23 formula).
experiments.specific_notes: Requires earnings/ex-div event data (Optionomics + Alpaca corporate actions) to be meaningful -- the whole point is the event-conditioned trade-off.

experiments.comparison: BC-2 (immediate CC after every assignment) vs. recovery-conditioned CC policy.
experiments.specific_notes: Directly tests one of the charter's own non-negotiable rules -- expected to confirm it, but the experiment is pre-registered rather than assumed.

experiments.comparison: BA-1 (mechanical close-before-assignment) vs. assignment-acceptable policy, with B6 (buy-and-hold assigned underlying) as an additional reference for whether active management post-assignment adds value beyond just holding.
experiments.specific_notes: Needs the ownership model's actual output (not just a proxy) to be meaningful -- this experiment is downstream of the ownership model existing (Phase 6).

experiments.comparison: BA-2 (unconditional hold-to-basis-recovery) vs. a pre-registered sweep of bounded recovery-wait policies (distinct max-wait-days / thesis-invalidation-trigger combinations, named before any OOS split is examined).
experiments.specific_notes: Selection happens ONLY on the purged walk-forward split; the winning candidate is then confirmed on a separate, previously untouched OOS split it was never evaluated against during selection (see H-A-04's failure_mode for the exact three-step protocol). H-A-02 (now the settled 'a bound must exist' constraint) has no experiment of its own -- it's verified by implementation inspection, not a backtest run.

experiments.comparison: B5 (random-entry null) vs. defined-risk spread structure, once Level 3 approval and the CSP/CC/Recovery archetypes' graduation are both confirmed.
experiments.specific_notes: Gated -- see hypotheses.json's gated_until field. This entry exists so the experiment is not forgotten, not because it should be run soon.
